speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are a newborn presenting with respiratory distress; please tell me, how old are you in days, and has your mother had a fever or been sick during your pregnancy?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, born at 33 weeks of gestation. The newborn is presenting with respiratory distress 2 hours after birth. The mother had an uneventful pregnancy until premature onset of labor. There was no significant prenatal care history mentioned.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you. Given your prematurity at 33 weeks and the onset of distress two hours after birth, I need to know if you have any history of meconium aspiration or if there were any complications during delivery. REQUEST TEST: Blood Gas Analysis; REQUEST TEST: CBC.

speaker: Doctor
text: The analysis suggests a potential meconium aspiration or transient tachypnea of the newborn. Have you noticed any greenish discoloration in the amniotic fluid during delivery, and are there any signs of chest retractions or grunting breathing right now? REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_X-Ray.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Respiratory distress. I also have Grunting, Intercoastal and subcostal retractions, Peripheral cyanosis.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS). The combination of prematurity at 33 weeks, onset of distress within two hours of birth, and the classic triad of grunting, intercostal/subcostal retractions, and cyanosis is highly indicative of surfactant deficiency.
